function.name: requests_get
function.description: Sends a GET request to the specified URL to retrieve weather data from the Open-Meteo API. Note that the provided function is in Python 3 syntax.

url.description: URL of the Open-Meteo API endpoint.

headers.description: Headers to include in the request. Each key-value pair represents a header field and its value.

Content-Type.description: The MIME type of the body of the request (used with POST and PUT requests).

Accept.description: Media type(s) that is/are acceptable for the response.

timeout.description: Maximum time in seconds to wait for the server to send data before giving up. This is a float type value.

params.description: Query parameters for the GET request.

latitude.description: Latitude of the location, positive for N and negative for S. This is a float type value.

longitude.description: Longitude of the location, positive for E and negative for W. This is a float type value.

elevation.description: Elevation in meters above sea level for the location. The default value represents no elevation downscaling.

auth.description: Authentication tuple for HTTP authentication, in the format (username, password).

cert.description: Path to the SSL client certificate file (.pem). A null value means no client certificate is used.

cookies.description: Dictionary of cookies to send with the request. Each key represents a cookie name.

proxies.description: Dictionary mapping protocol names to the URL of the proxy. Each key-value pair represents a protocol and its proxy URL.

stream.description: If True, the response should be streamed; otherwise, it should be downloaded immediately.

verify.description: Whether to verify the server's TLS certificate.

**Reykjavík – the clear winner** | Why Reykjavík stands out | What you’ll find | |---------------------------|------------------| | **Largest arena & most activity** – *Laugardalshöll* hosts the national team’s home games, international tournaments, and club matches. • Season ticket holders get priority seating
• On‑site skate rentals and coaching clinics | | **Convenient transport links** – Keflavík International Airport sits ~50 km away, and public buses run directly into town. From the airport you’re within a 30–40 minute drive to the arena. | • Airport shuttle services
• Bike rental options near the rink | | **Vibrant nightlife & culture** – After a game you can explore cafés, bars, museums, and the famous Harpa concert hall—all within walking distance. | • Live music venues
• Art galleries
• Local craft beer pubs | --- ### Other notable spots | City | Highlights for Hockey Fans | |------|-----------------------------| | **Akureyri** | • *Íþróttahúsin* – a modern multi‑sport complex with a decent-sized ice surface.
• Smaller crowds mean more intimate viewing experiences.
• Great base for exploring North Iceland’s fjords afterward. | | **Hafnarfjörður** | • Home to *HK Hafnarfjarðar*, a competitive junior program.
• Close enough to Reykjavík for day trips. | | **Kópavogur / Garðabær** | • Suburban arenas hosting youth leagues—good for family outings. | --- #### Quick Travel Checklist 1. **Tickets** - Buy online via the *Icelandic Ice Sports Federation* site or through the venue’s box office. 2. **Accommodation** - Book centrally located hotels or Airbnbs in Reykjavík for easy access to both the rink and tourist sites. 3. **Getting Around** - Public bus #55 runs between the airport and downtown. - Taxis and rideshare apps (Uber, Lyft) operate throughout the capital region. --- ### Bottom line If your goal is to soak up the atmosphere around top‑level Icelandic ice hockey while enjoying all the perks of a bustling capital, **Reykjavík** is unbeatable. For those who prefer a quieter setting yet still want solid hockey action, consider adding a stop in **Akureyri**, especially during the winter season when the northern lights add extra sparkle to evening games. Happy travels—and may the puck stay in play!
